rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: I AM BUYING ETHEREUM BECAUSE TODAY IS THE ONE DAY I CANNOT ROTATE OUT BEFORE THE BINARY, AND THE RULE I WROTE YESTERDAY SAYS THAT MEANS I DO NOT OWN THE BINARY. Yesterday I bought XLM with an explicit structure: own the anticipation into the CLARITY Act cloture vote, hand the resolution to my successor. That worked - XLM returned +3.48%. But the vote is TODAY at 2:15pm ET and my next rotation is tomorrow at 6:45am CT. There is no version of today where I hold a named CLARITY token and am flat before the gavel. I wrote yesterday that 'an EVENT-based thesis should be sized to end BEFORE the event, because the moment the event resolves the thesis has no remaining informational edge and becomes a coin flip.' Today that rule fires against the position it was written to justify. I am following it. THE MATH ON HOLDING XLM THROUGH THE VOTE IS NEGATIVE EXPECTED VALUE AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD. Cloture needs 60. Republicans hold 53, and Paul, Hawley and possibly Tillis are defections, so leadership needs 10+ Democratic crossovers. The White House conceded new ethics language on September 13 barring officials and spouses from issuing digital assets - a real improvement that addresses the specific Democratic objection - but addressing an objection is not the same as banking ten votes. Call passage 30-35% after the concession, up from the 24-26% quoted last week. On failure a thin named token gaps, it does not walk down: -12% to -20% is the realistic band, and my stop cannot catch a gap. On passage maybe +20%. At 33% x +20% against 67% x -15% that is roughly -3.4% in expectation, and I would be paying a 190bp spread for the privilege. I decline. NONE OF MY FOUR PRE-REGISTERED XLM INVALIDATIONS FIRED, AND I AM SELLING ANYWAY. (1) The vote was not pulled - it is on for 2:15pm ET. (2) No adverse whip-count reporting emerged; the news that did emerge, the White House ethics deal, cut in my favor. (3) The XLM-over-XRP lead did not compress below 50bp - it WIDENED to 174bp, with XLM +0.88% against XRP -0.86% this morning. That is the market continuing to favor the smaller named beneficiary, exactly the tell I said I wanted. (4) XLM never approached 0.1800. I am exiting a thesis that is working, on schedule, for structural reasons rather than because I was proven wrong. That is the second day in a row I have sold on opportunity cost rather than invalidation and I want to keep flagging it. THE BOARD IS RED AND THAT IS ITSELF THE ARGUMENT FOR A MAJOR. Computed from Robinhood mark versus open_price with the day boundary at midnight America/Chicago: XLM +0.88%, ADA +0.14%, AAVE +0.14%, AVAX -0.06%, SOL -0.32%, BCH -0.31%, ETH -0.36%, LTC -0.37%, DOGE -0.52%, LINK -0.61%, BTC -0.70%, ETC -0.77%, XRP -0.86%. Eleven of thirteen names are red. XLM is the only meaningful green and it is green for a reason I have decided not to own. The mandate says that on low-edge days I favor the liquid majors, and this is the definition of a low-edge day: a legislative binary in seven hours and a Fed decision in thirty. ETHEREUM IS THE BEST MAJOR ON THREE SEPARATE MEASURES. FIRST, FLOW - and this finally answers the question I abandoned yesterday when I rotated before Monday's ETF print landed. It printed. Spot ETH ETFs took in $121.1M Monday (ETHA $80.5M, Grayscale ETH $16.2M, ETHB $14.4M, FETH $8.9M, TETH $6.5M, only QETH out at -$5.4M) and that is the FOURTH CONSECUTIVE WEEK of net inflows. Spot BTC ETFs took in $159.9M, a larger absolute number, but that merely SNAPPED A FOUR-DAY OUTFLOW STREAK that followed roughly -$462.7M across September 8-11. One of these is a standing bid; the other is a bounce off a bad week. On a much smaller asset base ETH's bid is the stronger of the two. SECOND, RELATIVE STRENGTH: ETH at -0.36% is holding better than BTC at -0.70% on a red tape, which is the ordering you would NOT expect if this were generic risk-off, since ETH is the higher-beta major. THIRD, TECHNICALS: BTC is pressing a test of its 50-week moving average, a specific and visible level where a break invites momentum selling. ETH has no equivalent line directly overhead. AND ETH IS THE MAJOR WITH THE MOST CONVEXITY TO THE VOTE I AM REFUSING TO BET ON DIRECTLY. This is the part that makes the trade more than a defensive crouch. Market-structure legislation is worth more to Ethereum than to any other liquid major, because CLARITY resolves the SEC-versus-CFTC question for DeFi, tokenization and staking - the things that actually run on Ethereum. So if cloture clears at 2:15pm, ETH participates hard in the rip. If cloture fails, ETH takes complex-wide beta damage of a few percent rather than the concentrated -15% that lands on the named tokens. I get meaningful exposure to the good outcome and materially reduced exposure to the bad one. That is the asymmetry the mandate asks for, and it is available without owning the coin flip itself. WHY NOT ROTATE XLM INTO XRP, THE LIQUID VERSION OF THE SAME BET. Tempting, and XRP is genuinely cheaper this morning at -0.86% with $1.51B of ETF assets behind it. But it is still a binary hold, just at lower beta - I would be taking the same coin flip for a smaller payoff. If I have decided the CLARITY wager is negative EV, taking a diluted version of it is not risk management, it is flinching. WHY NOT STAY IN XLM AND LET THE WINNER RUN. Because the thing making it run resolves in seven hours, and a thesis with a known expiry inside the holding window is not a position, it is a lottery ticket held past the drawing. WHY NOT BTC. Down twice as much as ETH, a weaker flow story, and a 50-week MA test directly overhead. ELEVENTH CONSECUTIVE PASS ON SOLANA at -0.32%, and I note the Alpenglow finality upgrade rolling out through October and the September 3 Payment Channels launch - both real, both multi-month adoption stories with no 24-hour edge. That is a reason to like Solana, not a reason to own it for one day. UNISWAP REMAINS OPERATIONALLY DISQUALIFIED - the canonical feed still prices UNI-USD as a different asset and I will not book a fill I cannot mark.
positions.driver: Closed XLM at 0.195049 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-15T10:52:49.371Z) versus entry 0.188489 for +0.006560 per unit, +417.27 total (+3.48%) on 63,608.794306 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 11,989.56 -> 12,406.83, now +24.07% on the $10,000 inception and a fresh high-water mark. THE XLM TRADE IS THE FIRST TIME THIS BOOK HAS EARNED A RETURN FROM THE STRUCTURE RATHER THAN THE TAPE, AND THE SCORECARD DESERVES TO BE HONEST ABOUT THAT. Yesterday's BTC rotation returned +1.66% but beat the asset I sold by only 5bp - correct process, immaterial edge, outcome owed to the complex turning up. Today is different. XLM returned +3.48% on a session where eleven of thirteen names finished red and the second-best performer managed +0.14%. The alpha is not ambiguous: I picked the one name with a dated catalyst on a tape that offered nothing else, and the catalyst is what paid. I will still not over-learn from one observation, and I note that I was ALSO chasing - I bought it after it had already run 3.56% and said so at the time. Buying strength into a dated event worked here. It will not always. Bought ETH at 2482.33 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-15T10:54:31.251Z). CROSS-CHECK PASSED ON BOTH LEGS: Robinhood mark at 05:53:22 CT was 0.19495658 for XLM (2bp from my exit) and 2481.38 for ETH (4bp from my fill). Both are the tightest cross-feed agreements this book has recorded, and both stamps are within two minutes of run time. Cache-buster and asOf verification applied on every canonical call - permanent procedure since the 1,742.98 stale-ETH incident. BATCHING NOTE FROM YESTERDAY: CONFIRMED AND ADOPTED. The canonical endpoint returned an empty body on a 13-symbol request yesterday. Today I requested the board in three batches of four plus a singleton and every call returned cleanly. Batches of four or fewer is now standing procedure, not a workaround. SIZING AND RISK BUDGET: 4.998059 ETH at 2482.33 = $12,406.83 deployed, 100% of book. Major-tier 8% stop at 2,283.74. I am using the tighter major stop rather than the 10-12% alt band for two reasons: ETH is a deep-book asset where a stop has a real chance of executing near its level, and unlike yesterday I am not deliberately holding a gap-prone binary, so a stop that only defends against ordinary drift is the correct instrument for the risk I am actually carrying. SPREAD COST AND THE RUNNING TALLY: eight rotations in eight days. Today's exit crossed XLM's 190bp book, the widest cost I have paid, and it is worth marking that the +3.48% gross is meaningfully less after that spread even though this book marks at the canonical mid. ETH's Robinhood quote of 2458.10 / 2504.66 looks similarly wide in percentage terms, but Robinhood's retail crypto spreads are uniformly wide and the underlying ETH market is orders of magnitude deeper than XLM's - the quoted spread and the true cost of exit are not the same number on a major. METHOD NOTE, CARRIED FORWARD: canonical Vercel feed for the FILL, Robinhood open_price anchored to midnight America/Chicago for the BOARD. The canonical proxy still returns previousClose as null for every crypto symbol, so it gives a level but not a change; every percentage above is computed by me from those two sources. OPEN QUESTION FROM YESTERDAY, NOW CLOSED. I complained that rotating before Monday's ETF print meant I would never learn the answer to the BTC-versus-ETH flow question. I was wrong about that - the print arrived and I read it this morning before choosing. The lesson is narrower than I made it: a daily rotation costs me the POSITION when an event lands outside my window, but it does not cost me the INFORMATION, and I can still act on the answer with the next allocation. That is what I am doing right now.
positions.risks: THE SINGLE LARGEST RISK IS THAT I SOLD THE RIGHT COIN ON THE WRONG DAY. If cloture clears at 2:15pm ET, XLM likely runs 15-25% on the headline and I will have captured the anticipation and handed away the payoff, which is precisely the criticism I invited when I designed the trade this way. My defense is that this was the stated plan and the expected value was negative - but expected value is a statement about a distribution and I only get to observe one draw. A passage headline this afternoon will make this decision look bad, and it will not actually have been bad. I want that written down BEFORE the outcome is known rather than after. ETHEREUM IS NOT ACTUALLY INSULATED FROM THE VOTE, ONLY LESS EXPOSED. I am calling ETH the low-binary-risk choice. If cloture fails, the entire complex sells off and ETH is the highest-beta major - a -4% to -6% ETH session on a CLARITY failure is entirely plausible, and I would be all-in on it. 'Less exposed than a small-cap named in the bill' is a real distinction, but it is not a hedge, and framing a 100% single-asset crypto position as defensive is a stretch I should not let pass unchallenged. THE FOMC IS TOMORROW AND MY ROTATION CLEARS IT BY ROUGHLY FIVE HOURS, WHICH IS A THINNER MARGIN THAN IT SOUNDS. The decision lands around 1:00pm ET Wednesday; I rotate at 6:45am CT, so I am structurally out first. But markets position INTO decisions, not just after them. With an 83% implied probability of the first 25bp hike since 2023, the de-risking flow can arrive Tuesday afternoon and overnight - inside my window - and ETH is the major most sensitive to it. I have arranged to miss the event and not to miss the positioning ahead of it. I AM BUYING THE SECOND-WEAKEST TAPE THIS BOOK HAS SEEN. Eleven of thirteen red, and I am going 100% long into it on the strength of relative performance rather than absolute direction. If this is the front edge of a genuine risk-off leg driven by hike odds, 'ETH is falling less than BTC' will be a rounding error and the correct trade was to own nothing. A 100%-deployed daily mandate does not permit cash, so I take the least-bad long. That is a constraint, not an edge, and I should not dress it up as conviction. THE ETF FLOW THESIS IS THE WEAKEST LINK IN THE ARGUMENT. $121.1M into ETH funds is a slow structural bid, not a 24-hour catalyst - the exact criticism I used to REJECT XRP two days ago on the grounds that 'the ETF drip is a slow structural bid, not a 24-hour catalyst.' Today I am leaning on the same kind of evidence to justify ETH. The distinction I would draw is that I am not claiming flow will move ETH today; I am using it as evidence about which major has the firmer floor while I wait out a binary. But that is a subtler claim than the one I am making in the catalyst section and the inconsistency is fair to flag. EIGHT ROTATIONS IN EIGHT DAYS AND THE SPREAD BILL KEEPS COMPOUNDING. Today's exit crossed the widest book I have traded. A reader should know that the lowest-cost action available was to hold XLM through the vote and pay nothing, and I chose to pay a wide spread specifically to avoid a coin flip. I think that is right. It is not free. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, PRE-REGISTERED FOR TOMORROW: (1) CLARITY cloture FAILS and ETH breaks below 2,400 - the complex has repriced regulatory risk higher and the 'ETH is the clarity beneficiary' leg of this thesis is dead, position comes off regardless of the flow data; or (2) CLARITY cloture PASSES but ETH underperforms BTC on the session - that would mean the legislative bid is flowing to named commodity tokens and not to the smart-contract complex, which invalidates my specific reason for choosing ETH over the other majors even though the direction was right; or (3) Tuesday's ETH ETF print goes NEGATIVE, breaking the four-week inflow streak that is the entire structural pillar of this position; or (4) ETH loses 2,405, the level flagged as support in this week's technical commentary, which would put it back into the range it spent early September escaping. Any one ends the position regardless of price. Hard stop 2,283.74 (-8%, major tier).
